messages:
joel: quick heads-up: sampleapp reproed a generator stream that never resumes after token refresh. happens when refresh happens mid-stream and we trigger a retry.

maria: hmm, is this the same hang we've seen with context cancellation? or different (auth vs network)?

joel: different symptoms. flow: long-lived stream, token TTL expires, client auto-refreshes token, does a reconnect+retry. server accepts new auth but the generator state on server side duplicates and we end up with two partial streams and the client-side generator API doesn't pick the resumed one.

alex: can you paste the client-side trace from the sampleapp? especially the RetryPolicy path.

joel: sure. using go-sdk main branch at commit 0f9b2, sampleapp flags: `--mode=stream --auto-refresh=true --retry=on`. trace below:
```
[14:22:01] INFO generator: stream started
[14:52:01] DEBUG token expiry detected, fetching new token
[14:52:01] DEBUG opening new stream for retry
[14:52:02] DEBUG server ack received for original stream (late)
[14:52:02] DEBUG client abandoned original stream, waiting for resumed frames
# nothing arrives on resumed stream
# client ReadLoop blocked at recvFrame()
```

sam: why would server ack the original late? sounds like duplicate start was processed. we might need idempotency keys on StartGeneratorStream or a resume token.

maria: agreed. Python/JS SDKs use a `stream_id` that persists across reconnects; go's generator API intentionally hid those details. maybe we should expose a resume token in opts so the runtime can reconcile duplicates.

jeol: typo — joel :P.

joel: yes, sorry. bottom line: race between late ack and retry path. proposed fixes: (A) client attaches a stable resume_id in start metadata so server can merge; (B) client waits for final server ack before abandoning original stream; (C) stronger backoff to avoid immediate concurrent starts.

alex: I lean to (A) + (B). (A) fixes server-side duplication. (B) is safer for cancellation semantics. (C) is bandaid-y.

sam: implementation note: StartGeneratorStream currently returns an io.ReadCloser-like generator that closes on ctx.Done. But if we spawn a retry we need the old object to return an error quickly. ensure ctx cancel triggers early.

joel: for a quick mitigation I've patched sampleapp to expose `ResumeID: uuid.New().String()` in opts and server was able to merge streams in local dev.

maria: can you add a small comment in the SDK docs about resume semantics? users will wonder why we send resume ids. also add to Quickstarts: "long-lived streams + token refresh" section.

joel: opened tiny draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/4332 with ResumeID plumbing and a unit test that simulates dup-start.

dev-bot: PR #4332 CI queued (linux-amd64, windows-amd64, macos) :hourglass:

alex: also check auth retry path on Dedicated mode; routing differences might make the resume id necessary across frontends.

sam: +1 on tests. add an e2e where we force token expiry mid-stream and assert generator returns ErrAborted and then resumes with same resume id.

joel: one UX question: should resume id be automatic and hidden, or explicit in opts? making it automatic is easier for users, but leaks complexity if they want multiple parallel independent streams from the same client.

maria: default automatic, with opt override. default should be stable per-call (not per-client) and documented.

alex: also add telemetry tag `resume_used=true/false` to help us count occurrences in prod.

joel: added to PR. next steps: get review from runtime folks and then land. I'll add a note in sampleapp onboarding docs about "expect behavior when tokens rotate".

maria: great. after merge let's update quickstarts and add a short blurb in the SDK migration guide (v0.12.x -> v0.13) about generator resume behavior.

dev-bot: PR #4332 CI passed (all platforms) :white_check_mark:

sam: will pick up e2e tests for CI next sprint. resolving for now.

joel: thanks everyone — this was a nasty race to reproduce. saved a customer pain. :relieved:
